title: Chest pain that will not go away — sit still and call
applies_to: An adult with pain, tightness, or heaviness in the chest lasting more than a few minutes, or spreading to an arm, the neck, the jaw, or the back.

citations.source: European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First Aid
citations.section: Chest pain of suspected cardiac origin

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020

steps.text: Ask where the pain is, how long it has lasted, and whether it spreads to an arm, the neck, or the jaw.
Call for an ambulance now if it has lasted more than a few minutes. Say the words chest pain.
Stop them moving. Help them sit down on the floor, leaning back against something, with the knees bent.
Loosen tight clothing at the neck and the waist.
Ask whether a doctor has already given them something to take for chest pain. If so, help them take their own, exactly as the label on it says.
Keep them still. Keep talking to them calmly, even if they are frightened or angry.
Stay beside them. Keep checking that they are awake and breathing normally.
Unlock the door and move furniture out of the way so the crew can get to them.

do_not: Do not let them drive themselves, and do not drive them yourself if an ambulance can come.
Do not give them anything to eat or drink.
Do not let them walk up stairs or carry anything.
Do not decide it is only indigestion because they are young or fit.
Do not give them anything of yours to take.
escalate_if: They stop answering you and stop breathing normally — start pushing on the chest.
They go grey, sweaty, or sick, or say they feel they are about to die — say this on the phone at once.
The pain came on as a tearing feeling in the back — tell the crew those exact words.
They are short of breath as well, or their lips look blue — say so on the phone.
They faint, even for a moment — that changes how urgent this is.
